title: Agent Context Memory: A Governance-First Specification for AI Agent Context Memory
description:
What this is. A specification for governance-first context memory in autonomous AI agent systems.

The contribution. ACM recognizes that agent memory is fundamentally an authorization problem and applies established access control and audit-log patterns to this domain. The core contribution is the Mandate Gate: a pre-work mandate, confirmed by the principal, must exist in the agent's memory before work is a governed interval. Prior memory models (MemGPT, CoALA, Generative Agents) treat memory as a working resource the agent draws from during work. ACM treats memory as a precondition.

Core structure. Three memory tiers organized by trust level: Intent (principal-authored mandate), Trace (agent records, append-only) and Evidence (captured separately from the agent). Memory lives in a repository of its own and is bound to repositories of work by identity; scopes follow one rule (a folder holding a mandate, an orientation and records); shared recording uses one file per record with closed months sealed into one verifiable file. 25 numbered requirements each have a specified check and an evidence status (inherited, proposed, observed or deferred).

Relationship to PEA. ACM is the operationalization of Principles of Earned Autonomy (PEA) for the context memory design problem. PEA is the theory; ACM is the implementation standard for memory.

Claims. The specification claims no implementation conformance beyond the status stated for each requirement. It acknowledges RBAC/MAC and audit-log principles and cites CoALA (arXiv:2309.02427), Generative Agents (arXiv:2304.03442) and MemGPT (arXiv:2310.08560).

Relationship to AII. ACM states the memory structure that the agency-preservation boundary condition of Augmented Individual Intelligence (AII) would need.

Read in this order. README.md (overview), then SPEC.md (the full specification).
